edges.effect_quant: In a meta-analysis of 8 randomized trials involving 537 patients with recurrent or refractory C. difficile infection, fresh FMT lowered recurrent clinical diarrhea versus controls (RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.16-0.87); in the landmark NEJM trial, 13/16 patients (81%) responded after one infusion and 15/16 (94%) after up to two infusions versus 4/13 (31%) on vancomycin alone.
edges.population: mostly adults with recurrent or refractory Clostridioides difficile infection treated after failure of standard antibiotic approaches
edges.mechanism: FMT restores colonization resistance by reseeding depleted anaerobic gut communities, increasing microbial diversity, and suppressing recurrent C. difficile expansion after antibiotic-driven dysbiosis.
edges.summary: For recurrent C. difficile infection, FMT is one of the clearest microbiome-based therapeutic signals in clinical medicine. Randomized trials and pooled analyses consistently show markedly higher cure rates and lower recurrence than standard antibiotic-only management, although not every modern capsule protocol has outperformed placebo.
edges.caveats: Protocols differ by donor screening, route, fresh versus frozen material, and whether repeat dosing is used. A recent placebo-controlled capsule trial was neutral, so the strongest confidence still comes from the broader RCT and meta-analytic literature rather than any single contemporary formulation.
